title: Sorting Socks
question: How can we sort a jumble of socks?
coverAlt: Big and Little Wonderer: Sorting Socks

readAloud.say: (Pretend a soft sock lands in your lap.)

readAloud: Big Wonderer tips a basket of clean socks onto the rug. Little Wonderer sees stripes, dots, stars, and many colors.
A jumble is easier to understand when we choose one thing to notice. First they look at color. Blue socks go together. Yellow socks go together.

readAloud.ask: Can you point to two socks that share a color?

readAloud: Next they look at patterns. Stripes join stripes. Dots join dots. Stars join stars.
Then they compare size. A small sock may look like a big sock, but a matching pair needs the same size, color, and pattern.
Little Wonderer places each match side by side. Pair by pair, the jumble becomes tidy groups. One striped sock is left alone.

readAloud.ask: Where might its matching sock be?

readAloud: Big Wonderer finds it peeking from the empty basket. The last pair clicks together. Sorting helped them look closely and find every match.
steps: Read the story aloud together and stop at each “Ask”.
Print the pack and pick two or three pages; there is no need to do them all.
Point, circle, trace and color. Snip only with a grown-up.
Fold the picture book and read it again at bedtime.
